newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea to "positively" consider peace talks - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea to "positively" consider peace talks - Kyodo.

text.p: North Korea would "positively" consider joining proposed four-nation talks aimed at a permanent peace on the Korean Peninsula, a senior Pyongyang official was quoted as saying on Wednesday.

"We would positively consider four-way talks if they were to work in favour of peace and the reunification of the (Korean) peninsula," Hwang Jang-yop, secretary of the ruling Workers' (Communist) Party, told Japan's Kyodo news agency.

After offering an apology to South Korea in December over a submarine incursion, North Korea agreed to attend a preparatory joint briefing by U.S. and South Korean officials on the four-nation peace talks, which would also include China.
But the Stalinist state has put off attending the briefing this months.

"The joint briefing was postponed because in the process of negotiations there arose some problems that needed to be adjusted at working levels," said Hwang who was in Japan on a two-week visit to attend an international seminar.
Analysts believe North Korea put off attending the briefing pending a grain deal with the United States.

In January, Washington gave permission to Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc., the world's largest private grain trading company, to export 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to North Korea in what was expected to be a barter arrangement.
U.S. officials have told Reuters that North Korea has not made a direct link between successful completion of the Cargill deal and Pyongyang's participation at the peace talks briefing.
But they said North Korea may have thought it could get Washington to pick up some of the costs.
Hwang also suggested that North Korea's de facto leader Kim Jong-il would formally succeed his late father Kim Il-sung after the third anniversary of his death in July 1994.

"No schedule has been decided yet. But Secretary Kim has occasionally told us that it would be good to hold elections to choose top leadership mechanism after the three-year mourning," Hwang was quoted as saying.
Experts on North Korea in Japan consider Hwang a close adviser to Kim Jong-il.
The 54-year-old Kim has yet to be formally confirmed in two key posts held by his late father -- general secretary of the ruling Workers' Party and state president.
